name: webpack-config-require-in-callback
hook: require works inside webpack config callbacks even when next.config.js is ESM
body: Webpack config callbacks (the function passed to webpack:) run in Node.js at build time, not at config-file-load time. This means `require` is available inside the callback even when next.config.js uses ESM imports at the top level. This allows accessing Next.js's bundled webpack modules via `require('next/dist/compiled/webpack/webpack.js')` from inside the callback.
why: Next.js 15's next.config.js is ESM at the top level, but webpack bundling happens at runtime in Node.js. The callback is evaluated by Node.js directly, not by an ESM module loader. This is the bridge between the ESM config file and CommonJS webpack internals.

name: napi-rs-canvas-webpack-external-conflict
hook: @napi-rs/canvas as webpack external string conflicts with minify-webpack-plugin
body: Adding '@napi-rs/canvas' (as a string) to webpackConfig.externals causes minify-webpack-plugin to throw `_webpack.WebpackError is not a constructor` during the minification phase. This is a conflict between how the externalized package is handled and how minify-webpack-plugin constructs errors internally in Next.js's bundled webpack. The fix is to NOT add it to webpack externals — serverExternalPackages in Next.js config handles externalization at a different level that does not trigger this conflict.
why: The minify-webpack-plugin built into Next.js's webpack bundle calls `new WebpackError()` internally. When @napi-rs/canvas is marked as an external, the plugin's error construction logic appears to receive something it doesn't expect, causing the constructor error. Using serverExternalPackages instead avoids this because webpack doesn't process those packages at all during bundling.

name: resolve-alias-cannot-intercept-node-protocol
hook: resolve.alias cannot intercept node: URL scheme imports — use NormalModuleReplacementPlugin
body: webpack resolve.alias uses exact string matching (or $ suffix for exact match), but it does NOT interpret regex patterns. A key like '^node:' or '\.node$' in resolve.alias will match literal module names, not node: URL scheme imports. To intercept `node:crypto`, `node:fs`, etc., you must use `NormalModuleReplacementPlugin` (a ResolvePlugin) which webpack calls for every module resolution. The plugin class is accessible via `require('next/dist/compiled/webpack/webpack.js')` → init() → webpack.webpack.NormalModuleReplacementPlugin.
why: The `node:` protocol is a separate resolution path in webpack 5 from module name resolution. resolve.alias operates on module names (the string after 'node:' in 'node:crypto'), not on the 'node:' prefix itself. Only a ResolvePlugin can intercept the full request string including the protocol.
